title: The Hot Big Bang
description: Everything we see was once hotter and denser than the inside of any star, and has been expanding and cooling ever since. The Friedmann equations of general relativity say how fast: by what fills the universe and how it is curved. The first study of the Origin.

puzzle.goal: A homogeneous, isotropic universe is described by one scale factor a(t) that stretches every distance. Put such a space into general relativity: the square of the expansion rate H = (da/dt)/a is set by the density ρ of what fills it, by the curvature k of space, and by a vacuum energy Λ. Write the square of the expansion rate.
puzzle.name: First Friedmann equation
puzzle.ask: A flat universe (k = 0) without Λ has exactly the critical density ρ_c = 3H²/(8πG). With H in units of 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹ and G in 10⁻¹¹ SI units, find ρ_c in units of 10⁻²⁷ kg/m³ (about five protons per cubic metre).
puzzle.method: Treat a comoving ball of dust: its kinetic energy per unit mass ½ȧ² minus the potential 4πGρa²/3 is constant, and that constant is the curvature. General relativity adds the vacuum term.
